name: New Objectivity photography
summary: Sharp, close, frontal pictures of plants, tools, faces and machines, made in Germany between the wars. The camera sees more than the eye, and it names things without comment.

philosophy.core_thesis: The lens is exact and unsentimental, so the honest picture shows the structure of a thing at close range and in full detail.
design_principles: Fill the frame with one object, shot at 0.3 to 1m, so that its structure becomes the pattern.
Use a 135mm to 210mm lens on a 9×12cm or 13×18cm plate, stopped down to f/32 for full sharpness.
Light from one side in open shade or a window, with a key-to-fill ratio of 2:1.
Place the subject frontal and centred, or in strict rows, with a neutral grey or white ground.
Print on glossy paper at grade 2 and show the whole tonal scale without toning.
Repeat the same view for a whole series of 20 to 100 plates, so that the differences become the content.
anti_patterns: Soft focus, mist or hand-worked negatives
Captions that tell the viewer how to feel

composition.framing: Tight and frontal; the object touches or leaves the frame edges.
composition.viewpoint: Level with the subject, 0.3 to 1m away, camera square to the plane.
composition.geometry: Rows, spirals and repeats; the plant or tool forms its own grid.
composition.subject_placement: Centred, with a plain ground that takes 10–20% of the frame.

principles.rule: Let 1 object fill 80–95% of the frame; nothing else takes more than 5%.
Put the axis of the plant or tool at 0.5 of the width, within 0.03.
Repeat a leaf, rib or tooth at a constant pitch, with 8 to 20 repeats across the frame.
Keep 10–20% of the frame as plain grey or white ground.
Show 20 to 100 plates of one view and one light, and change only the specimen.

light.quality: Soft, even and directional: open shade or a north window.
light.direction: From one side, 60° to the lens axis, with a white card on the other side.

lens_and_camera.format: Plate or sheet film, 9×12cm to 13×18cm; digital medium format as a modern equivalent
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus on the nearest edge of the structure and tilt nothing; the depth of field covers 0.3m or more.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Neutral black and white with a full tonal scale, no toning and no grain.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a neutral mix (R 30, G 59, B 11).
Set the black point at 2% and the white point at 97%.
Apply +10% midtone contrast with a gentle S-curve.
Sharpen at radius 0.8px, amount 80%, to show the fine structure.
Add no grain and no vignette.
Do not crop; keep the edge of the plate.
colour_and_grade.grain: None: a fine-grain plate, sharp at 10× enlargement

subject_and_staging.staging: Minimal. The object stands on a plain ground; sitters face the lens and hold the pose for 1 to 2s.
subject_and_staging.direction: Say nothing about meaning. Ask the sitter to look at the lens with a neutral face.

workflow: Develop in a fine-grain developer, for a gamma of 0.7.
Contact print or enlarge to grade 2 on glossy paper.
Order the plates in a sequence by form.
Print the series at one size.
post_processing.output: A sharp glossy print of one view, shown with its siblings as a series or a book plate.

emotion.target_response: Cool attention: the viewer studies the thing and trusts the frame.

use_cases: product catalogues with a scientific feel
avoid_when: The brief needs warmth, mood or a story in one frame.
The subject is a moving crowd.

modifiers.how: Switch to a soft-focus lens at f/5.6, a platinum or gum print and a 40–60% mist; keep a single subject.
Use a 4×5 or digital medium format camera in colour at 1.5 to 20m, flat grey light and a fixed frontal view for 20 or more prints.
